characters.name: Georgiana Darcy

recaps.ending: Lady Catherine confronts Elizabeth after hearing a rumor that she may marry Darcy, but Elizabeth refuses to promise that she will reject him. Darcy learns of this resistance and gains hope that Elizabeth's feelings have changed. When he and Bingley return to the neighborhood, Bingley proposes to Jane and is accepted. Darcy then tells Elizabeth that his love remains unchanged; she admits that her judgment of him has altered and accepts his proposal. Elizabeth explains herself to the astonished Mr Bennet and persuades him that she truly respects Darcy. Elizabeth and Darcy marry and live at Pemberley, while Jane and Bingley also marry and settle nearby. Lydia and Wickham remain financially careless and frequently seek help. Georgiana grows close to Elizabeth, the Gardiners are warmly welcomed at Pemberley, and even Lady Catherine eventually resumes contact despite her anger at the match.
recaps.in_short: Elizabeth Bennet dislikes the wealthy Mr Darcy after his cold behavior and becomes increasingly prejudiced against him through the charming officer George Wickham. Darcy, meanwhile, falls in love with Elizabeth despite his objections to her family. His first proposal fails because he speaks arrogantly and Elizabeth blames him for separating Jane Bennet from Charles Bingley and for mistreating Wickham. Darcy's explanatory letter forces her to reconsider both men. Their warmer meeting at Pemberley is interrupted when Lydia Bennet runs away with Wickham, threatening the whole family. Darcy secretly finds the pair and pays the costs that make their marriage possible. Once Elizabeth learns what he did, her respect becomes love. Bingley returns and marries Jane. After Elizabeth withstands Lady Catherine's attempt to prevent a match, Darcy proposes again and she accepts. Elizabeth and Darcy marry with a clearer understanding of themselves and each other.

recaps.text: Mr Bingley rents Netherfield Park, exciting Mrs Bennet because she hopes he will marry one of her five daughters. At a local assembly Bingley is friendly and devotes himself to Jane, while his richer friend Darcy refuses to dance with Elizabeth and appears proud. Elizabeth treats the insult lightly but forms a strong dislike of him. Jane is invited to Netherfield, becomes ill after riding there in the rain, and stays with Bingley's sisters. Elizabeth walks to nurse her, giving Darcy an opportunity to observe her intelligence and confidence. His interest grows, though Caroline Bingley mocks Elizabeth and her family. Jane and Elizabeth return to Longbourn with the attraction between Jane and Bingley promising well.

The Bennet household receives Mr Collins, the cousin who will inherit Longbourn. Determined to marry a Bennet daughter, he transfers his attention from Jane to Elizabeth. The sisters also meet the handsome officer George Wickham. Wickham tells Elizabeth that Darcy denied him the church career intended for him by Darcy's father, confirming her bad opinion of Darcy. At the Netherfield ball, Elizabeth endures an awkward dance with Darcy, embarrassing behavior from her family, and Mr Collins's attentions. Jane and Bingley still appear deeply attached, but social differences and the conduct of Jane's relatives trouble Darcy and Bingley's sisters.

Mr Collins proposes to Elizabeth and cannot initially believe her refusal. Mrs Bennet is furious, but Mr Bennet supports his daughter. Collins soon proposes to Charlotte Lucas, who accepts because the marriage offers security; Elizabeth is dismayed by her friend's choice. Bingley and his party abruptly leave Netherfield for London, and Caroline writes as if he will not return. Jane tries to hide her pain. Elizabeth suspects Bingley's friends have deliberately separated the couple. During a London visit Jane receives little warmth from Caroline, strengthening that suspicion. Elizabeth later accepts Charlotte's invitation to visit her new home beside Rosings Park, where Mr Collins serves Lady Catherine de Bourgh.

At Hunsford, Elizabeth meets the overbearing Lady Catherine and again encounters Darcy, who is visiting Rosings. His frequent calls puzzle her. Colonel Fitzwilliam lets slip that Darcy recently saved a friend from an unsuitable marriage, and Elizabeth realizes that he helped separate Bingley from Jane. Darcy unexpectedly proposes, declaring love while emphasizing the inferiority of Elizabeth's connections. Angry at his manner, his interference with Jane, and Wickham's story, she refuses him. The next day Darcy gives her a letter. He explains that Jane seemed indifferent and that Wickham squandered his inheritance, then attempted to elope with Darcy's young sister for her fortune. Elizabeth recognizes weaknesses in her own judgment and begins to reassess both Darcy and herself.

Elizabeth returns home and tells Jane enough of Darcy's letter to correct their view of Wickham. She later travels with the Gardiners to Derbyshire. Believing Darcy absent, they tour Pemberley, where his housekeeper describes him as a generous master and brother. Darcy arrives unexpectedly but behaves with striking courtesy, introduces Elizabeth to Georgiana, and welcomes the Gardiners. Elizabeth's feelings soften as she sees him in his own surroundings. The visit ends when Jane's letters report that Lydia has run away with Wickham. Since the pair are unmarried and missing, scandal threatens every Bennet sister. Darcy hears the news, and Elizabeth leaves convinced that the disgrace has destroyed any possibility between them.

Mr Bennet and the Gardiners search for Lydia and Wickham. Mr Gardiner eventually reports that the couple have been found and will marry if Wickham's debts and financial demands are settled. The Bennets assume Mr Gardiner has paid heavily to save them. Lydia returns as a heedless bride and accidentally reveals that Darcy attended her wedding. Mrs Gardiner then tells Elizabeth the truth: Darcy located the fugitives, paid Wickham's debts, purchased his commission, and arranged the marriage, insisting on secrecy. Elizabeth understands that he acted largely for her sake. News that Bingley and Darcy have returned to Netherfield raises new hope, though neither gentleman immediately explains his intentions.

Bingley renews his courtship of Jane and proposes; she accepts. Lady Catherine arrives at Longbourn to demand that Elizabeth deny rumors of an engagement to Darcy. Elizabeth refuses to surrender her freedom or promise never to marry him. Her defiance gives Darcy reason to hope, and during a walk he again declares his love. Elizabeth now acknowledges her own love and accepts him. They discuss the misunderstandings, pride, and prejudice that kept them apart, and Darcy explains that Elizabeth's rejection changed his conduct. Mr Bennet gives consent after Elizabeth convinces him of her respect for Darcy. Elizabeth and Darcy marry and make Pemberley their home; Jane and Bingley marry as well, while the Gardiners remain valued members of their family circle.

characters.description: The second Bennet daughter, intelligent, observant, and quick to find humor in other people's behavior. She is close to her elder sister Jane and meets her parents' very different temperaments with affection mixed with impatience.
characters.name: Elizabeth Bennet

characters.description: Mr Bingley's wealthy friend, first seen at the Meryton assembly. His reserved manner, refusal to dance with unfamiliar women, and dismissive remark about Elizabeth make him appear proud and immediately earn her dislike.
characters.name: Fitzwilliam Darcy

characters.description: The eldest Bennet daughter and Elizabeth's closest confidante. Beautiful, gentle, and inclined to think well of everyone, she is her mother's chief hope for a favorable marriage.
characters.name: Jane Bennet

characters.description: The sociable young man who rents Netherfield Park. At his first local assembly he dances readily, treats his new neighbors warmly, and shows particular admiration for Jane Bennet.
characters.name: Charles Bingley

characters.description: The father of five daughters and master of Longbourn. Clever, sarcastic, and fond of withdrawing to his library, he often answers his wife's agitation with teasing rather than practical engagement.
characters.name: Mr Bennet

characters.description: The Bennet sisters' anxious, talkative mother, whose overriding ambition is to see her daughters married securely. News of an eligible bachelor at Netherfield immediately sends her into plans for an introduction.
characters.name: Mrs Bennet

characters.description: The youngest Bennet sister, lively, confident, and eager for amusement. She and Kitty delight in the militia officers stationed near Meryton and pursue every opportunity to encounter them.
characters.name: Lydia Bennet

characters.description: The most studious Bennet sister. She seeks distinction through reading, moral observations, music, and other accomplishments, though her wish to display them often exceeds her social judgment.
characters.name: Mary Bennet

characters.description: Elizabeth's sensible friend and the eldest daughter of the Bennets' neighbors, the Lucases. She joins Elizabeth in observing the newcomers and discussing the behavior displayed at the Meryton assembly.
characters.name: Charlotte Lucas

characters.description: Mr Bennet's clergyman cousin and the man due to inherit Longbourn. Formal, self-important, and eager to appear conciliatory, he arrives intending to repair relations with the family and speaks constantly of his patroness.
characters.name: William Collins

characters.description: A handsome, engaging newcomer to the militia. His easy manners make a strong impression on Elizabeth, while a tense chance meeting shows that he and Darcy already know one another.
characters.name: George Wickham

characters.description: Charles Bingley's fashionable unmarried sister and a member of the Netherfield household. She welcomes Jane into her company, though Elizabeth is less persuaded by her polished friendliness.
characters.name: Caroline Bingley

characters.description: Mr Collins's wealthy and titled patroness at Rosings Park. Before she appears in person, Collins presents her as the source of his position and praises her attention to every part of his household and parish.
characters.name: Lady Catherine de Bourgh

characters.description: Mrs Bennet's intelligent and warm-hearted sister-in-law, visiting Longbourn from London. She is close to Jane and Elizabeth and offers them the measured concern and guidance often missing from their parents.
characters.name: Mrs Gardiner

characters.description: Mrs Bennet's brother, a London businessman whose good sense and courteous manners make him a trusted relation of the Bennet sisters. He and his wife take an active interest in their nieces' welfare.
characters.name: Mr Gardiner

characters.description: Darcy's much younger sister, whom Elizabeth meets at Pemberley. She is shy, gentle, and eager to please, quite unlike the proud and accomplished figure Elizabeth had been led to imagine.
characters.name: Georgiana Darcy

recaps.ending: Darcy's role in finding Lydia and paying the costs needed for her marriage to Wickham is revealed to Elizabeth through Mrs Gardiner. Bingley returns to Netherfield, renews his attentions to Jane, and becomes engaged to her. Lady Catherine visits Elizabeth to forbid a rumored match with Darcy, but Elizabeth refuses to promise that she will never accept him. When Lady Catherine repeats the confrontation to Darcy, Elizabeth's refusal gives him hope. Elizabeth thanks him for helping Lydia, and he tells her his feelings remain unchanged. His second proposal is accepted. They discuss how his pride and her prejudice distorted their first impressions and how both have changed. Mr Bennet consents once convinced that Elizabeth respects Darcy. Jane and Bingley marry and later live near Pemberley; Elizabeth becomes mistress of Pemberley and a loving sister to Georgiana. Kitty benefits from spending more time with her elder sisters, Mary remains at home, and Lydia and Wickham continue to need financial help. The Gardiners retain a close place in Elizabeth and Darcy's life.
recaps.in_short: Elizabeth Bennet meets the wealthy, reserved Fitzwilliam Darcy after his friend Charles Bingley rents Netherfield and falls in love with Elizabeth's sister Jane. Darcy's pride and a slight at their first assembly make Elizabeth dislike him, while the charming George Wickham gives her a false account of Darcy's cruelty. Darcy separates Bingley from Jane and later proposes to Elizabeth in a manner that emphasizes her inferior connections; she angrily refuses. His explanatory letter exposes Wickham's misconduct and forces her to reconsider her own prejudice. After Darcy behaves generously at Pemberley, Elizabeth begins to love him, but her sister Lydia's flight with Wickham threatens the family. Darcy secretly arranges their marriage. Bingley returns and marries Jane. When Lady Catherine tries to prevent Elizabeth from marrying Darcy, Elizabeth refuses to promise she will reject him. Encouraged, Darcy proposes again and is accepted. Their marriage rests on hard-won self-knowledge, while Jane and Bingley also settle happily nearby.

recaps.text: The Bennet family of Longbourn has five unmarried daughters, and Mrs Bennet is delighted when the wealthy bachelor Charles Bingley rents nearby Netherfield Park. Mr Bennet quietly makes the required visit despite teasing his wife about it. At the Meryton assembly, Bingley proves friendly and dances twice with the beautiful eldest daughter, Jane. His richer friend Fitzwilliam Darcy appears handsome but aloof; after refusing to dance with Elizabeth Bennet and slighting her within earshot, he becomes an object of her amused dislike. Jane and Bingley continue to admire one another, though Jane's calm manner conceals the strength of her feelings. Bingley's sisters cultivate Jane, while Elizabeth doubts their sincerity. As the neighborhood discusses the newcomers, Darcy begins noticing Elizabeth's intelligence and expression. She remains unaware of his growing interest and refuses him a dance when an opportunity arises at the Lucases' gathering.

Charles Bingley's arrival at Netherfield has brought the Bennets into close contact with his party. Jane and Bingley are mutually attracted, while Elizabeth dislikes Darcy for his proud behavior even as he becomes increasingly interested in her. When Jane rides to Netherfield in bad weather at her mother's urging, she falls ill and must remain there. Elizabeth walks across muddy fields to nurse her, provoking disdain from Bingley's sisters but admiration from Darcy. Several days in the same house sharpen the contrast between Elizabeth's lively independence and Caroline Bingley's efforts to impress Darcy. Elizabeth and Darcy repeatedly debate manners, vanity, and character, each alert to the other's judgments. Mrs Bennet visits and embarrasses Elizabeth by speaking too openly of Jane's prospects. Once Jane recovers enough to travel, the sisters return to Longbourn. Elizabeth leaves convinced that Darcy is disagreeable, while his attraction has deepened despite his objections to her family's position and conduct.

Jane and Bingley's attachment has grown, while Darcy's interest in Elizabeth remains hidden behind exchanges she reads as argumentative. Mr Bennet's cousin William Collins arrives at Longbourn: he is a pompous clergyman, heir to the estate, and tireless admirer of his patroness, Lady Catherine de Bourgh. In Meryton, Elizabeth meets the charming militia officer George Wickham. He claims Darcy deprived him of the church career intended for him by Darcy's father, confirming Elizabeth's worst assumptions. At the Netherfield ball, Wickham is absent, Darcy unexpectedly asks Elizabeth to dance, Collins makes himself conspicuous, and Mrs Bennet loudly anticipates Jane's marriage. Soon afterward, Collins proposes to Elizabeth. She refuses firmly despite her mother's pressure. He then turns to Elizabeth's practical friend Charlotte Lucas, who accepts him for the security of a home, shocking Elizabeth. Meanwhile Bingley leaves for London, and Caroline writes that the whole Netherfield party will remain there while hinting that Bingley may marry Darcy's sister. Jane is hurt but still unwilling to suspect deliberate interference.

After Bingley leaves Netherfield, Jane visits London but receives a cool response from Caroline and no visit from Bingley. Elizabeth concludes that his friends have separated him from Jane. She later travels to Kent to visit Charlotte, now managing marriage to Mr Collins with practical skill. At nearby Rosings, Lady Catherine questions Elizabeth with intrusive authority. Darcy and his cousin Colonel Fitzwilliam arrive to visit their aunt. Darcy frequently calls at the parsonage and meets Elizabeth on her walks, but his intentions remain unclear. Fitzwilliam casually reveals that Darcy recently saved a friend from an unsuitable marriage, and Elizabeth realizes he was responsible for separating Bingley and Jane. Soon afterward Darcy proposes to her. He declares strong feelings but dwells on her inferior connections and on the struggle required to offer marriage. Elizabeth rejects him, accusing him both of ruining Jane's happiness and of cruelly mistreating Wickham. Darcy is astonished and asks whether her answer might have been different without his insulting manner; she tells him his conduct had already fixed her opinion of him.

After Elizabeth rejects Darcy, he gives her a letter answering her charges. He admits persuading Bingley that Jane was indifferent, but says he acted from honest concern and from objections to the Bennet family's behavior. He also explains that Wickham squandered his inheritance, then tried to elope with Darcy's fifteen-year-old sister Georgiana for her fortune. Elizabeth recognizes how prejudice and wounded pride shaped her judgment. Back home, she tells Jane part of the truth but cannot prevent Lydia from going to Brighton with the militia. Elizabeth later tours Derbyshire with the Gardiners and visits Pemberley only after being assured Darcy is absent. His housekeeper's praise and his estate unsettle her former picture of him. Darcy unexpectedly returns and treats Elizabeth and her relations with striking courtesy. She meets the shy Georgiana, while Caroline Bingley unsuccessfully tries to revive old resentments. The changed relationship is abruptly interrupted by letters from Jane: Lydia has run away with Wickham, apparently without marrying him. Elizabeth tells Darcy and leaves at once, believing her family's disgrace has ended any possibility between them.

Lydia's flight with Wickham throws the Bennet family into crisis. Mr Bennet and Mr Gardiner search in London while Mrs Bennet collapses into agitation. Mr Gardiner eventually reports that the couple have been found and will marry if Mr Bennet settles modest financial terms. Mr Bennet assumes his brother-in-law must have paid a much larger hidden sum, and Elizabeth regrets that Wickham will now be permanently connected to the family. Lydia returns to Longbourn as a heedless bride, pleased with her status and indifferent to the harm she caused. She accidentally mentions Darcy's presence at her wedding. Elizabeth asks Mrs Gardiner for an explanation and learns that Darcy found Lydia and Wickham, paid Wickham's debts, secured his commission, and arranged the marriage. He acted quietly, accepted Mr Gardiner's public credit, and said he was responsible because he had concealed Wickham's character. Elizabeth now understands the full extent of Darcy's generosity and realizes that her feelings for him have changed, though she has no reason to believe he still wishes to marry her.

Darcy secretly rescued the Bennets from Lydia and Wickham's scandal, and Elizabeth now loves him, though neither knows the other's present feelings. Bingley and Darcy return to Netherfield. Bingley resumes his courtship of Jane and proposes; she accepts, bringing joy to both families. Lady Catherine then arrives at Longbourn after hearing a rumor that Darcy may marry Elizabeth. She demands a promise that Elizabeth will refuse him, arguing that family inferiority and an intended match with her own daughter make the union impossible. Elizabeth refuses to bind herself. Lady Catherine reports this defiance to Darcy, but it gives him hope that Elizabeth's feelings may have changed. During a walk, Elizabeth thanks him for saving Lydia. Darcy renews his proposal, and she accepts. They acknowledge their earlier errors: his pride and reserve, her quick judgment, and the misunderstandings that followed. Mr Bennet gives consent after Elizabeth assures him she truly respects Darcy. Jane marries Bingley and lives near Pemberley; Elizabeth marries Darcy and forms a close bond with Georgiana. Lydia and Wickham remain improvident, Kitty improves through her sisters' influence, and the Gardiners are warmly welcomed at Pemberley.

characters.name: Elizabeth Bennet

characters.name: Jane Bennet

characters.name: Mr Bennet

characters.description: The excitable mother of the five Bennet daughters. With the family estate destined to pass to a male cousin, she regards finding prosperous husbands for her daughters as an urgent practical mission and greets news of an eligible neighbour with immediate enthusiasm.
characters.name: Mrs Bennet

characters.description: The youngest Bennet sister, self-assured and eager for dances, officers, and any source of amusement. Her high spirits are encouraged by her mother and only lightly checked by her father.
characters.name: Lydia Bennet

characters.description: An unmarried young gentleman who rents Netherfield Park. His considerable income, friendly temper, and readiness to join local society make him an immediate object of interest to the Bennet household before they have even met him.
characters.name: Charles Bingley

characters.name: Fitzwilliam Darcy

characters.name: Caroline Bingley

characters.name: Charlotte Lucas

A ceremonious letter announces his wish to visit and make peace with the family, while also displaying his solemn self-importance and devotion to his noble patroness.
characters.name: William Collins

characters.name: George Wickham

characters.name: Lady Catherine de Bourgh

characters.name: Mr Gardiner

characters.description: Elizabeth and Jane's intelligent, warm-hearted aunt. Formerly resident near Derbyshire, she is an affectionate adviser to her nieces and takes a clear-eyed interest in Elizabeth's acquaintance with Wickham.
characters.name: Mrs Gardiner

characters.name: Georgiana Darcy

recaps.ending: Bingley returns to Netherfield and, once assured of Jane's affection, asks her to marry him. Lady Catherine then visits Elizabeth to demand that she promise never to accept Darcy, but Elizabeth refuses. Learning of this refusal gives Darcy hope that Elizabeth's feelings have changed. During a walk he renews his proposal, and she accepts, acknowledging how completely her opinion of him has altered. They explain the misunderstandings that divided them: Darcy believed Jane indifferent to Bingley, while Elizabeth had trusted Wickham's account and judged Darcy through her first resentment. Mr Bennet consents after satisfying himself that Elizabeth truly loves Darcy, and Mrs Bennet is delighted by the match. Jane and Bingley marry, as do Elizabeth and Darcy. The Bingleys later move nearer to Pemberley, Elizabeth grows close to Georgiana, and the Gardiners remain welcome visitors. Lydia and Wickham continue to live beyond their means and seek help from their relations, while Lady Catherine eventually resumes contact with her nephew despite her anger at his marriage.
recaps.in_short: Elizabeth Bennet meets the wealthy but aloof Fitzwilliam Darcy after his friend Charles Bingley rents Netherfield and falls in love with Elizabeth's sister Jane. Elizabeth's dislike of Darcy deepens when the charming officer George Wickham accuses him of cruelty. Darcy unexpectedly proposes, but she rejects him for his pride, his role in separating Jane and Bingley, and his alleged treatment of Wickham. His explanatory letter exposes Wickham's misconduct and forces Elizabeth to reconsider her judgments. Visiting Darcy's estate, she sees his generosity and meets him again on warmer terms, but her sister Lydia's elopement with Wickham threatens the whole family. Darcy secretly finds the couple and finances their marriage. Bingley returns and becomes engaged to Jane. After Elizabeth refuses Lady Catherine's demand that she reject Darcy, Darcy proposes again and Elizabeth accepts. The two couples marry, while Lydia and Wickham remain improvident and dependent on family assistance.

recaps.text: The Bennets of Longbourn have five unmarried daughters and an estate that will pass to a male cousin, making their future security uncertain. Mrs Bennet is delighted when the rich bachelor Charles Bingley rents nearby Netherfield Park. At a local assembly Bingley is sociable and clearly admires the eldest daughter, Jane, while his still wealthier friend Fitzwilliam Darcy appears proud and refuses to dance with Elizabeth Bennet. Elizabeth responds to the slight with amused dislike. Jane and Bingley continue to enjoy one another's company, though Jane's reserve makes her feelings easy to underestimate. When Jane becomes ill during a visit to Netherfield, Elizabeth walks there and remains to nurse her. Her independence and intelligence increasingly attract Darcy, even as Caroline Bingley mocks Elizabeth's country connections and tries to secure Darcy's attention for herself. Elizabeth notices his interest but interprets his manner through the poor impression he made at their first meeting.

Jane recovers and the Bennet sisters return home. Mr Collins, the pompous clergyman who will inherit Longbourn, arrives intending to repair relations with the family and, privately, to choose one of the daughters as a wife. In Meryton the sisters meet George Wickham, a handsome militia officer who shows immediate unease when Darcy appears. Wickham tells Elizabeth that Darcy unjustly denied him the church career intended for him by Darcy's late father. The story confirms Elizabeth's existing prejudice, and Wickham's easy manners make her ready to trust him. At the Netherfield ball, Wickham is absent but Elizabeth must dance with Darcy; their strained conversation reinforces her dislike. Collins embarrasses the Bennets by his obsequious attention to Darcy and his public solemnity, while Mrs Bennet speaks openly of Jane's expected marriage. Jane and Bingley remain attached, but the behaviour of several members of Jane's family gives Darcy and Bingley's sisters reason to oppose the match.

Mr Collins proposes to Elizabeth, confidently treating her refusal as modest encouragement until Mrs Bennet demands that Mr Bennet force her to accept. Mr Bennet instead supports Elizabeth's decision. Collins soon transfers his attention to Charlotte Lucas, who accepts him for the security of a home despite having no romantic expectations. Elizabeth is shocked by her friend's practical choice. Bingley abruptly leaves Netherfield for London, and Caroline writes as though he will not return and hopes to marry Darcy's sister. Jane is deeply hurt but continues to think well of everyone involved. During a London visit she calls on Caroline, whose cold response reveals that the friendship was insincere. Elizabeth concludes that Bingley's sisters and Darcy have separated the couple. Meanwhile Wickham's attentions shift to a young woman who has recently inherited money, weakening Elizabeth's personal hopes without yet changing her belief in his account. Elizabeth travels with Sir William and Maria Lucas to visit the married Collinses at Hunsford, near Lady Catherine de Bourgh's estate at Rosings.

At Hunsford, Elizabeth sees that Charlotte manages her marriage by arranging the household to minimize Mr Collins's company. Lady Catherine receives the visitors at Rosings and questions Elizabeth with commanding curiosity. Darcy arrives with his cousin Colonel Fitzwilliam and repeatedly visits the parsonage. Fitzwilliam casually reveals that Darcy recently saved a friend from an unsuitable marriage, confirming to Elizabeth that Darcy separated Bingley from Jane. Darcy then proposes to Elizabeth, declaring his love while dwelling on the inferiority of her family. She rejects him and accuses him both of ruining Jane's happiness and of mistreating Wickham. The next morning Darcy gives her a letter. He explains that he believed Jane did not love Bingley and objected to the impropriety of her relatives. He also states that Wickham rejected a promised church living for money, spent it, and later tried to elope with Darcy's fifteen-year-old sister for her fortune. Reviewing past events, Elizabeth recognizes inconsistencies she ignored and admits that vanity and prejudice distorted her judgment of both men.

Elizabeth returns to Longbourn with a transformed private opinion of Darcy, though she tells Jane only what is necessary about Wickham. Lydia is invited to Brighton with the colonel's wife and the militia. Elizabeth warns her father that Lydia's unchecked behaviour may bring disgrace, but he allows the trip because it promises temporary quiet at home. Elizabeth later tours Derbyshire with the Gardiners. Believing Darcy absent, they visit Pemberley, where the housekeeper's affectionate account presents him as a generous master and brother. Darcy unexpectedly appears and treats Elizabeth and her relations with striking courtesy. He calls on them, introduces Elizabeth to his shy sister Georgiana, and encourages further meetings between the two parties. Elizabeth begins to understand that she could have respected and loved him, while Darcy's altered manner suggests that her rejection prompted serious self-examination. Their renewed acquaintance is warm but still unsettled, and neither has spoken directly about the proposal or the letter.

News arrives that Lydia has run away from Brighton with Wickham, apparently without marrying him. Elizabeth tells Darcy and immediately leaves with the Gardiners, convinced that the scandal has ended any possibility between them. Mr Bennet and Mr Gardiner search in London. Wickham's debts and lack of intention to marry become clear, but Mr Gardiner eventually reports that the couple have been found and that Wickham will marry Lydia in exchange for financial arrangements that seem unusually favourable. Mr Bennet assumes his brother-in-law has paid a large sum. Lydia and Wickham visit Longbourn after the wedding. Lydia remains heedless of the harm she caused and accidentally mentions that Darcy attended the ceremony. Mrs Gardiner's answering letter reveals that Darcy located the fugitives, paid Wickham's debts, purchased his military commission, and arranged the marriage, asking that his role remain secret. Elizabeth understands that he acted for her sake as well as for Lydia and the family, deepening both her gratitude and her affection.

Bingley and Darcy return to Netherfield. Bingley renews his courtship of Jane and proposes, to the joy of both Jane and Mrs Bennet. Lady Catherine then arrives at Longbourn after hearing a rumour that Darcy may marry Elizabeth. She demands that Elizabeth deny any engagement and promise never to accept him, arguing that Darcy is intended for her daughter. Elizabeth refuses to surrender her freedom of choice. Lady Catherine reports the encounter to Darcy, but Elizabeth's refusal to renounce him gives him reason to hope. On a walk, Darcy again declares his love, and Elizabeth accepts him. They discuss the changes since his first proposal: he has tried to correct his arrogance, while she acknowledges the prejudice encouraged by wounded pride and Wickham's deception. Darcy confirms that he separated Bingley and Jane because he misread Jane's reserve, and that he later corrected the mistake. Mr Bennet gives his consent after Elizabeth assures him of her love. Jane marries Bingley and Elizabeth marries Darcy. Elizabeth settles at Pemberley, becomes close to Georgiana, and welcomes the Gardiners, while Lydia and Wickham remain financially unstable and repeatedly seek assistance from their better-established relations.

characters.description: The second of the five Bennet daughters, intelligent, lively, and confident in her judgment of character. She values wit and independence and is ready to resist both social pressure and a marriage without respect.
characters.name: Elizabeth Bennet

characters.description: The eldest Bennet sister, admired for her beauty and gentle temper. She habitually interprets others generously and is immediately drawn to the amiable new tenant of Netherfield.
characters.name: Jane Bennet

characters.description: The ironic, bookish father of five daughters. His estate is entailed away from them, but he often retreats into mockery rather than addressing the family's financial and social vulnerability.
characters.name: Mr Bennet

characters.description: The excitable mother of the Bennet daughters, whose overriding ambition is to marry them securely before their father's death leaves them without Longbourn. Her public enthusiasm frequently embarrasses Elizabeth and Jane.
characters.name: Mrs Bennet

characters.description: A wealthy, friendly young man who rents Netherfield Park. Open in manner and easily pleased, he admires Jane Bennet from their first dance.
characters.name: Charles Bingley

characters.description: Bingley's wealthy friend and the owner of Pemberley. His reserve and consciousness of rank make him appear proud at the local assembly, where Elizabeth overhears him dismiss her as an undesirable dance partner.
characters.name: Fitzwilliam Darcy

characters.description: Bingley's fashionable unmarried sister. She cultivates Darcy's attention and treats Jane politely while looking down on the Bennet family's connections.
characters.name: Caroline Bingley

characters.description: Elizabeth's sensible, pragmatic friend. At twenty-seven with little fortune, she views marriage chiefly as a route to security and advises Jane to make her affection easier for Bingley to see.
characters.name: Charlotte Lucas

characters.description: Mr Bennet's pompous cousin and the heir to Longbourn. A clergyman under the patronage of Lady Catherine de Bourgh, he makes a conciliatory visit while repeatedly praising his patron and his own social judgment.
characters.name: William Collins

characters.description: A handsome militia officer with easy manners and an apparent connection to Darcy's family. His visible tension with Darcy and friendly interest in Elizabeth immediately excite her curiosity.
characters.name: George Wickham

characters.description: The youngest Bennet sister, fifteen, impulsive and absorbed in officers, gossip, and amusement. Her parents' weak supervision allows her confidence to exceed her judgment.
characters.name: Lydia Bennet

characters.description: The formidable mistress of Rosings Park, Darcy's aunt and Mr Collins's patron. Accustomed to directing everyone around her, she expects deference to her wealth, rank, and opinions.
characters.name: Lady Catherine de Bourgh

characters.description: Darcy's younger sister, a shy and accomplished girl whom Elizabeth meets at Pemberley. Her warmth toward her brother contrasts with the forbidding family pride Elizabeth had expected.
characters.name: Georgiana Darcy

characters.description: Mrs Bennet's sensible brother, a London tradesman whose manners disprove Darcy's assumptions about Elizabeth's relations. He and his wife give Jane and Elizabeth practical affection and guidance.
characters.name: Mr Gardiner

characters.description: Elizabeth's warm, perceptive aunt. She cautions Elizabeth against an imprudent attachment to Wickham and later takes her on the journey that brings them to Derbyshire.
characters.name: Mrs Gardiner

When he and Elizabeth walk together, he renews his proposal and she accepts, each acknowledging the errors that distorted their earlier judgments. Mr Bennet consents once assured Elizabeth truly respects Darcy, and Mrs Bennet celebrates the fortune. Jane marries Bingley and lives near Elizabeth and Darcy at Pemberley. Darcy, meanwhile, falls in love with her despite objecting to her family's conduct. He separates his friend Bingley from Elizabeth's sister Jane, then proposes to Elizabeth while emphasizing her inferior connections. She refuses and condemns both actions. Darcy's explanatory letter exposes Wickham's attempt to elope with Darcy's young sister and makes Elizabeth reconsider her judgments. Meeting Darcy again at Pemberley, she sees his generosity and changed manners. When Lydia Bennet runs away with Wickham, Darcy secretly pays for their marriage, saving the family. After Elizabeth defies Lady Catherine's demand that she reject Darcy, Darcy proposes again; Elizabeth accepts, and they marry with genuine understanding and respect.

recaps.text: The wealthy Charles Bingley rents Netherfield near the Bennet family, whose five daughters must marry well because their home is entailed to a male cousin. Mrs Bennet eagerly pursues the new neighbor. At the local assembly, Bingley is friendly and dances repeatedly with the beautiful Jane Bennet. His friend Fitzwilliam Darcy appears arrogant, refuses local introductions, and declines to dance with Elizabeth Bennet while she is close enough to hear his slight. Elizabeth turns her wounded pride into amusement and readily believes the neighborhood's poor opinion of him. Jane and Bingley grow interested in each other, while Bingley's sister Caroline and Darcy privately criticize the Bennet family's lesser connections.

Jane falls ill while visiting Netherfield, and Elizabeth walks there to nurse her, arriving muddy and provoking Caroline Bingley's contempt. Darcy becomes increasingly attracted to Elizabeth's intelligence and lively expression, though their conversations remain combative. After Jane recovers, the sisters return home. Mr Collins, Mr Bennet's pompous cousin and heir, arrives intending to marry a Bennet daughter as compensation for inheriting Longbourn. In Meryton the younger sisters meet the militia officer George Wickham. Darcy and Wickham react tensely on seeing each other, and Wickham's charm immediately interests Elizabeth. Her existing prejudice against Darcy makes her ready to hear Wickham's account of their history.

Wickham tells Elizabeth that Darcy denied him the church career promised by Darcy's late father, presenting Darcy as jealous and unjust. At the Netherfield ball, Elizabeth is disappointed by Wickham's absence, endures an awkward dance with Darcy, and is embarrassed by her family's conspicuous behavior. Mr Collins proposes to Elizabeth and cannot initially believe her firm refusal. He soon proposes to her practical friend Charlotte Lucas, who accepts for financial security despite having no romantic attachment. Bingley unexpectedly leaves Netherfield for London, and Caroline writes that the party will not return and implies that Bingley should marry Darcy's sister. Jane is hurt but remains charitable. Elizabeth believes Bingley's friends have deliberately separated him from Jane.

Jane visits London but Caroline Bingley avoids her, confirming Elizabeth's suspicion that Bingley's sisters oppose the match. Elizabeth visits Charlotte and Mr Collins in Kent, where she meets his commanding patron Lady Catherine de Bourgh and encounters Darcy, Lady Catherine's nephew. Darcy seeks Elizabeth's company with increasing frequency, behavior she finds puzzling. His cousin Colonel Fitzwilliam accidentally reveals that Darcy recently saved Bingley from an unsuitable marriage. Darcy then proposes to Elizabeth, declaring passionate love while dwelling on the inferiority of her family. She refuses him, accusing him of ruining Jane's happiness and mistreating Wickham. Darcy is shocked by both her rejection and her view of his character.

Darcy gives Elizabeth a letter explaining that he separated Bingley from Jane because Jane's reserve looked like indifference and because of the Bennet family's conduct. He also reveals that Wickham rejected a church living for cash, squandered it, and later tried to elope with Darcy's fifteen-year-old sister Georgiana for her fortune. Elizabeth recognizes that vanity and prejudice made her trust Wickham and misread Darcy. Back home, she cannot fully warn her family without betraying Darcy's confidence. Lydia is invited to Brighton with the militia, and Elizabeth urges her father to stop the reckless trip, but he dismisses the danger. Traveling later with the Gardiners, Elizabeth visits Pemberley only after believing Darcy absent. The housekeeper's praise and the estate's responsible management deepen her revised opinion, just before Darcy unexpectedly appears.

At Pemberley, Darcy treats Elizabeth and the Gardiners with striking courtesy and introduces Elizabeth to Georgiana. Elizabeth begins to imagine that she may have forfeited a valuable relationship. News then arrives that Lydia has run away with Wickham without any confirmed marriage. Elizabeth tells Darcy, assuming the scandal will end his interest, and returns home. Mr Gardiner and Mr Bennet search while the family fears lasting disgrace. Mr Gardiner eventually reports that the couple have been found and will marry if Mr Bennet agrees to a surprisingly modest settlement. Lydia and Wickham visit Longbourn after the wedding. Lydia carelessly reveals that Darcy attended the ceremony, and Mrs Gardiner's letter tells Elizabeth that Darcy found the pair, paid Wickham's debts, bought his commission, and arranged the marriage while trying to conceal his role.

Elizabeth understands that Darcy intervened for her sake as well as from responsibility toward Wickham. Bingley and Darcy return to Netherfield, and Bingley soon proposes to Jane, who accepts. Lady Catherine visits Longbourn after hearing a rumor that Darcy may marry Elizabeth and demands a promise that Elizabeth will refuse him; Elizabeth rejects her authority and makes no such pledge. Lady Catherine reports the confrontation to Darcy, but Elizabeth's refusal gives him hope. Darcy proposes again, and Elizabeth accepts, explaining that her feelings have entirely changed. They acknowledge his former arrogance, her mistaken judgments, and the letter that began their growth. Darcy explains that he encouraged Bingley once he understood Jane's affection. Mr Bennet gives thoughtful consent and Mrs Bennet rejoices. Jane and Bingley marry, and Elizabeth becomes mistress of Pemberley, where she and Darcy build a marriage based on love, respect, and corrected understanding.

Encouraged, Darcy proposes again and is accepted. Their marriage rests on hard-won self-knowledge, while Jane and Bingley also settle happily nearby.

Jane and Bingley are mutually attracted, while Elizabeth dislikes Darcy for his proud behavior even as he becomes increasingly interested in her. When Jane rides to Netherfield in bad weather at her mother's urging, she falls ill and must remain there. Once Jane recovers enough to travel, the sisters return to Longbourn. Elizabeth leaves convinced that Darcy is disagreeable, while his attraction has deepened despite his objections to her family's position and conduct.

Jane and Bingley's attachment has grown, while Darcy's interest in Elizabeth remains hidden behind exchanges she reads as argumentative. Mr Bennet's cousin William Collins arrives at Longbourn: he is a pompous clergyman, heir to the estate, and tireless admirer of his patroness, Lady Catherine de Bourgh. In Meryton, Elizabeth meets the charming militia officer George Wickham. Soon afterward, Collins proposes to Elizabeth. She refuses firmly despite her mother's pressure. He then turns to Elizabeth's practical friend Charlotte Lucas, who accepts him for the security of a home, shocking Elizabeth. She later travels to Kent to visit Charlotte, now managing marriage to Mr Collins with practical skill. At nearby Rosings, Lady Catherine questions Elizabeth with intrusive authority. Darcy and his cousin Colonel Fitzwilliam arrive to visit their aunt. Darcy frequently calls at the parsonage and meets Elizabeth on her walks, but his intentions remain unclear. Fitzwilliam casually reveals that Darcy recently saved a friend from an unsuitable marriage, and Elizabeth realizes he was responsible for separating Bingley and Jane. Soon afterward Darcy proposes to her. He declares strong feelings but dwells on her inferior connections and on the struggle required to offer marriage. Elizabeth rejects him, accusing him both of ruining Jane's happiness and of cruelly mistreating Wickham. Darcy is astonished and asks whether her answer might have been different without his insulting manner; she tells him his conduct had already fixed her opinion of him.

After Elizabeth rejects Darcy, he gives her a letter answering her charges. He admits persuading Bingley that Jane was indifferent, but says he acted from honest concern and from objections to the Bennet family's behavior. He also explains that Wickham squandered his inheritance, then tried to elope with Darcy's fifteen-year-old sister Georgiana for her fortune. Elizabeth recognizes how prejudice and wounded pride shaped her judgment. Back home, she tells Jane part of the truth but cannot prevent Lydia from going to Brighton with the militia. Elizabeth later tours Derbyshire with the Gardiners and visits Pemberley only after being assured Darcy is absent. His housekeeper's praise and his estate unsettle her former picture of him. Darcy unexpectedly returns and treats Elizabeth and her relations with striking courtesy. She meets the shy Georgiana, while Caroline Bingley unsuccessfully tries to revive old resentments. The changed relationship is abruptly interrupted by letters from Jane: Lydia has run away with Wickham, apparently without marrying him. Elizabeth tells Darcy and leaves at once, believing her family's disgrace has ended any possibility between them.

Lydia's flight with Wickham throws the Bennet family into crisis. Mr Bennet and Mr Gardiner search in London while Mrs Bennet collapses into agitation. Mr Gardiner eventually reports that the couple have been found and will marry if Mr Bennet settles modest financial terms. Mr Bennet assumes his brother-in-law must have paid a much larger hidden sum, and Elizabeth regrets that Wickham will now be permanently connected to the family. Lydia returns to Longbourn as a heedless bride, pleased with her status and indifferent to the harm she caused. She accidentally mentions Darcy's presence at her wedding. Elizabeth asks Mrs Gardiner for an explanation and learns that Darcy found Lydia and Wickham, paid Wickham's debts, secured his commission, and arranged the marriage. He acted quietly, accepted Mr Gardiner's public credit, and said he was responsible because he had concealed Wickham's character. Elizabeth now understands the full extent of Darcy's generosity and realizes that her feelings for him have changed, though she has no reason to believe he still wishes to marry her.

Darcy secretly rescued the Bennets from Lydia and Wickham's scandal, and Elizabeth now loves him, though neither knows the other's present feelings. Bingley and Darcy return to Netherfield. Bingley resumes his courtship of Jane and proposes; she accepts, bringing joy to both families. Lady Catherine then arrives at Longbourn after hearing a rumor that Darcy may marry Elizabeth. She demands a promise that Elizabeth will refuse him, arguing that family inferiority and an intended match with her own daughter make the union impossible. Elizabeth refuses to bind herself. Lady Catherine reports this defiance to Darcy, but it gives him hope that Elizabeth's feelings may have changed. During a walk, Elizabeth thanks him for saving Lydia. Darcy renews his proposal, and she accepts. They acknowledge their earlier errors: his pride and reserve, her quick judgment, and the misunderstandings that followed. Mr Bennet gives consent after Elizabeth assures him she truly respects Darcy. Jane marries Bingley and lives near Pemberley; Elizabeth marries Darcy and forms a close bond with Georgiana. Lydia and Wickham remain improvident, Kitty improves through her sisters' influence, and the Gardiners are warmly welcomed at Pemberley.
